question.worked_solution:
First, we isolate the ${u}^{2}$ on one side of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}^{2}+\frac{2}{5} & =\frac{1}{2} \\ {u}^{2} & =\frac{1}{2}-\frac{2}{5} \\ {u}^{2} & =\frac{5}{10}-\frac{4}{10} \\ {u}^{2} & =\frac{1}{10}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we take the square root of both sides of the equation and solve the resulting absolute value equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{{u}^{2}} & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{10}} \\ |u| & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{10}} \\ |u| & =\frac{\sqrt{1}}{\sqrt{10}} \\ |u| & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} \\ u & =\pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}
$$
